boundary: This is a quantized lattice-amplitude noisy theorem. Arbitrary real amplitudes, analog calibration drift, saturation, correlated noise, and a practical high-rate decoder remain open.
decoder_program: Round incidence measurements and the two weighted channels to Delta-units. Solve min support(z) subject to D z=s and w_j z=m_j (or congruent modulo p), |z_i|<=K, support<=7. Exact uniqueness guarantees at most one feasible minimizer.
model: error e=Delta*z with z integer, support(z)<=7, |z_i|<=K; additive measurement noise has infinity norm <Delta/2 before componentwise rounding

modular_mode.comment: This assumes the weighted accumulation is performed modulo p before or within readout; it is an architecture requirement, not an analog free lunch.
modular_mode.uniqueness_condition: 2K < p; invertible cycle/theta responses mod p then exclude every nonzero difference of two K-bounded seven-sparse errors

noise_margin: strict <Delta/2 componentwise is a deterministic adversarial guarantee for lattice-amplitude errors
rounding_theorem: All incidence and moment rows are integer. Rounding y/Delta recovers the exact integer syndrome and moments whenever ||noise||_infinity<Delta/2. The inherited stacked spark>=15 then gives a unique support<=7 integer error.
